summary: Environment A direct binary verification for the Phase 6.1 Windows rebuild (Operator Ergonomics: keyboard shortcuts for the Needs Attention queue). This is a frontend-only change, so this evidence file documents both what direct binary inspection could and could not confirm, honestly.

installer.note: The SHA-256 and file size both changed from the Phase 5.4 baseline, confirming a genuinely new artifact was packaged - not a stale/copied installer.

dllPresenceCheck.method: Extracted the installer with 7z and confirmed all three bundled runtime DLLs are present at the installer root.

rustSymbolRegressionCheck.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings/nm against the extracted cip-desktop.exe, re-checking every prior-phase Rust-side symbol/string this project's manifest already tracks, to confirm zero Rust regression (this phase touched zero Rust files).
rustSymbolRegressionCheck.conclusion: Every previously-tracked Rust-side symbol/string count is byte-for-byte identical to the Phase 5.4 baseline - confirms zero Rust-side regression, consistent with this phase changing only TypeScript/TSX files.

frontendTextSearchLimitation.attempted: Searched the extracted cip-desktop.exe for the new shortcut-legend text this phase adds (the literal substring 'for the first item', part of shortcutLegend's output, e.g. 'A = Display, R = Reject for the first item').
frontendTextSearchLimitation.controlExperiment: To rule out a build defect versus a tooling limitation, also searched for two other frontend-only strings known to be present in the source and UNCHANGED by this phase: the literal heading text 'Needs Attention' and the literal button label 'Display'. Both ALSO returned 0 matches, despite being present in every prior Windows build's frontend bundle including this one.
frontendTextSearchLimitation.conclusion: This is a strings(1)/nm(1) tooling limitation, not a build defect: Tauri embeds the built frontend (dist/) bundle into cip-desktop.exe in a compressed form its bundler produces, so plain byte-string scanning cannot find frontend-only literal text at all - not even long-standing, unchanged text. This was not previously documented in this project's evidence because no prior phase attempted to verify frontend-only literal text via strings; every prior frontend-affecting phase (e.g. Phase 3.8.7.8's Bible Display shortcut) instead verified via the frontend test suite plus a build/bundle-hash change, which is the same approach this phase's evidence relies on below.
correctnessEvidenceUsedInstead: Fresh Vite build produced a new asset bundle hash for this rebuild (dist/assets/index-*.js), distinct from the Phase 5.4 build's bundle - proving a genuinely new frontend bundle was embedded, not a stale one.

Full frontend test suite: 231/231 passing (220 pre-existing + 11 new, covering resolveUnifiedShortcutAction and shortcutLegend across every domain's action shape) - see pilot-evidence/6.1/build/keyboard-shortcuts-evidence.json.
Installer SHA-256 and file size both changed from the Phase 5.4 baseline (see installer block above), confirming the newly-built bundle was genuinely packaged into this installer.
npm run build (tsc -b && vite build) completed with zero errors as part of the same build pipeline that produced this exact installer (see the build task's own log: 'built in 766ms').

architectureVerification.outerInstallerStub: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, Nullsoft Installer self-extracting archive - standard NSIS bootstrapper, unchanged from every prior phase.
architectureVerification.installedApplicationBinary: cip-desktop.exe: PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64, confirmed genuinely x64.

conclusion: This phase's Rust-side surface is unchanged (confirmed via unchanged symbol/string counts) and this phase's frontend-side surface is a genuinely new, fully-tested bundle (confirmed via a fresh build hash, a changed installer SHA-256, and a full 231/231 test pass) - but direct strings-based verification of the new frontend text itself is not possible against Tauri's compressed embedded bundle, a real tooling limitation documented here rather than worked around with a fabricated match.
